title: Pre-Market — Friday Nov 20, 2026
html:
Pre-Market Briefing · Friday, November 20, 2026 · options expiration day

The AI selling didn't stop for the night: Nasdaq futures are down about 1.6%, and Anthropic is giving back its debut pop.

Here's what I'm seeing before the bell. The S&P 500 starts the day under its 200-day average for the first time since spring, and the selling overnight was in exactly the same place it was yesterday afternoon: chips, AI hardware and the companies that own pieces of AI labs. Oil, bonds and the dollar barely moved. This is a positioning problem in one trade, not a macro scare.

What matters this morning

  • Futures: S&P 500 E-minis −0.76% and Nasdaq 100 E-minis −1.63% at 4:57 a.m. ET (Reuters); SPY is $710.70 pre-market (−0.7%). The Dow is roughly flat to −0.2%: the selling is in tech, not everywhere.
  • The AI unwind kept going overnight: Anthropic (ANT) $89.01 (−8.4% from Thursday's $97.17 close), NVDA $142.21 (−2.6%, under yesterday's 52-week low), AMD −6.5%, BE −7.6%, DELL −5.7%, CRDO −5.3%, VRT −4.7%, SMH −3.2%.
  • Waller speaks at 8:25 a.m. ET. On Wednesday he said "you have to go 50 in December." Futures already price a December hike at about 98% (CME FedWatch via Reuters), so the question is size, not direction.

| - Monthly options expiration today, plus the December WTI contract expires: expect prices to get pulled toward big strikes into the close. |

Top 3 actionable

  • OXY Dec 18 $55 put (idea, in the entry zone): OXY $53.46, under your 1.382 ($54.20); stop line $56.30, target $47.79 → 2.0 to 1 from here. Last quote $2.65/$2.87, OI 5,416. IV 32.6% vs moves 32.7% → FAIR.
  • AAPL Dec 18 $360 call (idea, in the entry zone): AAPL $350.30 pre-market (+0.3%), $2.60 over the $347.70 stop line, target $360.83 → 4.0 to 1. Last quote $5.00/$5.50 (9.5% spread, right at the limit), OI 34,359. IV 23.7% vs 22.1% → FAIR. The one name on the list holding its trend.

| - AMZN Dec 18 $245 put: the trigger ($255) broke pre-market, but at $252.22 it's too late at this price (0.8 to 1). The entry that works: a bounce to $255–256 that fails on a 15-minute close (2.2 to 1). |

Futures from Reuters (4:57 a.m. ET); yields, WTI, gold, VIX and bitcoin from Yahoo Finance's pre-market board; ETFs from Webull pre-market. I couldn't confirm Asia and Europe index figures this morning; Dow Jones headlined the session "global markets fall as tech-bubble jitters resurface."

What the combination says. Stocks lower, yet the 10-year barely moved (5.05%), oil slipped, the dollar was flat and gold fell another 2.6%. When gold and bitcoin fall alongside tech on a fear day, people are raising cash, not hiding. That confirms last night's force #1 (an AI positioning flush) and leaves force #2 (a Fed hiking into slower data) unchanged: bonds aren't pricing a growth scare, so there's no rate relief coming for expensive tech.

My read: the open is lower and tech-led, and I expect the first push down to get bought somewhere between Thursday's low and the 50% line, because options expiration tends to pin. I'm only moderately sure of that bounce. What would change my mind: the Nasdaq futures losses widening after Waller, or NVDA losing $140 in the first 30 minutes. Then the bounce isn't coming today.

What's going on

1. The AI unwind: stronger overnight

Evidence. Reuters at 4:57 a.m.: Nasdaq 100 E-minis −434 points (−1.63%); Nvidia −2.6%; AMD, Broadcom, Marvell and Micron −3.5% to −5.5%; CoreWeave and Nebius down more than 5%; Amazon, Meta and Microsoft each down more than 1.8%. Anthropic slid 6.8% early and is $89.01 on Webull now, $6 above its $83 offer price. Reuters says the Nasdaq is 13.6% under its Oct 6 record and the indexes are on track for their worst week since April 2025. Its reasons: worries over data-center spending, borrowing costs and Jensen Huang's departure.

What it means. The selling that started around Anthropic's first trade kept going in the overnight session with no new news. That's the tell of a crowded trade being cut, not a reaction to a headline. It supports the NVDA, PLTR, AMZN and INTC put ideas and hurts anything long AI. What would prove me wrong: NVDA back over $148.80 and ANT holding above $92.72 (its debut-day low).

2. The Fed: unchanged, still hawkish

Evidence. Philadelphia Fed President Anna Paulson said Thursday the Fed "will need to raise interest rates again because inflation is too high" (Reuters). Goolsbee called inflation "way higher" than 2% on Thursday. FedWatch shows about 98.4% odds of a December hike. Waller is first up at 8:25 a.m.; Cook at 12:15 p.m.

What it means. The hike is priced. A Waller repeat of "50 in December" would push the 2-year up and hit IWM and long-duration tech; a softer word ("25 and see") could be the spark for an expiration-day bounce. What would prove me wrong: the 10-year jumping over 5.10% with stocks down. That would turn a positioning flush into a rates problem.

3. Oil and gold: weaker

Evidence. WTI (Dec) $81.67 (−0.9%) and Brent −1.6%, heading for a third weekly loss as Hormuz shipments are back near pre-war levels (Reuters). The December WTI contract expires today. Gold $3,590 (−2.6%) after −2.7% Thursday.

What it means. Softer oil helps the OXY put idea and does nothing for XOM's bounce case. Gold falling two days in a war-and-fear tape is the joke the market is telling: the oldest safe haven is being sold to cover the newest crowded trade.

S&P 500 at the open

Under the 200-day, heading for the 50% line

Key: dashed = Fib levels, solid red = neckline/stop line, colored lines = 14/30/50/200-day averages (purple 14, orange 30, blue 50, black 200), gold line = pre-market price (implied from SPY's −0.7%; the index itself doesn't trade pre-market).

Levels: 7,416 Thu high · 7,350 Nov 5 low (neckline) · 7,348 200-day · 7,261 38.2% of the Mar 30 → Oct 6 run · 7,174 Thu low · ~7,124 pre-market · 7,081 50% · 6,900 61.8%.

Game plan. If the S&P opens above 7,261 (the 38.2%), the overnight selling got absorbed: put ideas tighten stops, and AAPL's call idea is the one to watch. If it holds between 7,081 and 7,261, expect expiration-day chop with Thursday's low (7,174) as the pivot; trade only the setups already in the entry zone. If it opens below 7,081 (the 50% line), the next stop is the 61.8% near 6,900, and every bounce is a chance to set up puts, not buy.

The chart shows the double top that broke on Nov 17 and Thursday's close under the 200-day (7,348) on a bearish outside day. Price is now under every average I track; the 50 over the 200 is the last bullish thing on it, and that gap is shrinking.

Movers on your list

NVDA $142.21 pre-market · −2.6%

Levels: $170.22 your 0.786 · $155.33 your 0.5 · $148.80 stop line (Nov 12 low) · $140.93 target 1 · $133.10 target 2.

Why. No new Nvidia news overnight; it's trading with the chip complex (Reuters: AMD, Broadcom, Marvell, Micron −3.5% to −5.5%). The House briefing requests (Dec 1–2) and the CEO vacancy stay unresolved.

Bull case: RSI under 20 and a stock 30% under its 200-day can snap back hard; a reclaim of $148.80 would trap the late shorts. Bear case: your levels failed in order (1.382, 0.786, 0.5), the bounce Thursday failed at the old 0.5, and price is under all six averages. I side with the bear case, but target 1 is $1.28 away.

What it means for the plan from last night: the NVDA $140 put idea is near target 1 ($140.93). For a new entry it's too late at this price (0.2 to 1). The entry that works: a bounce to $147–148.50 that fails under $148.80 on a 15-minute close.

AMZN $252.22 pre-market · −2.0%

Levels: $275.22 your 2.618 · $264.43 2.382 · $258.60 stop line · $255.00 trigger · $246.95 2.0 (target 1) · $229.47 1.618.

Why. Reuters: Amazon, Meta and Microsoft each down more than 1.8% pre-market as the AI-capex worry spreads; Amazon owns about 15% of Anthropic, which is down 8%.

Bull case: the 200-day ($245.03) and the 2.0 ($246.95) sit just under price, a strong floor zone. Bear case: rejected twice under the 2.618, lost the 2.382, and now trading under the 25/30/50-day band ($255–257.56). I lean bear, but the floor is close.

What it means: the trigger is crossed pre-market, but from $252.22 the reward to target 1 is $5.27 against $6.38 of risk. Too late at this price. The play is a failed bounce into $255–256.

If every idea in play hit its stop today (one contract each: NVDA, PLTR, BA, AAPL, OXY, INTC), the paper loss would be about $1,700 from Thursday's closing marks. No new plays this morning: nothing overnight created a setup that passes 1.5 to 1 from where prices are now.

Option quotes are Thursday's closing quotes from Webull; they will reprice at the open. Verify in Webull before acting.

Alerts for today

NVDA — price crosses above $148.80 → the put idea's stop line; below $140.93 → target 1 AMZN — price crosses above $255.00 → the failed-bounce entry zone is live (wait for the 15-minute close back under) AAPL — price crosses below $347.70 → the call idea's stop line OXY — price crosses above $56.30 → the put idea is wrong S&P 500 — below 7,081 → the 50% line is going; 6,900 is next

An alert means look now, not buy now.

Opening rule of the day

Let the first 30 minutes settle on a gap-down expiration day. The open will be full of forced hedging, and the first move often reverses before 10 a.m. Never chase a put into a target that's a dollar away (NVDA today); wait for the bounce, then act on the 15-minute close.

All research: Market Desk
